preamble: Palatalization (secondary palatalization or 'softening') raises the body of the tongue toward the hard palate during the articulation of a consonant, typically before front vowels or a palatal glide. It is phonemic in East Slavic languages such as Russian and in the Goidelic broad–slender system of Irish, automatic before front vowels in Lithuanian, and arises morphologically in Romanian, where plural -i surfaces as palatalization of a final consonant. It recurs across several Indo-European branches (Slavic, Baltic, Celtic, Romance) and is among the most widespread secondary articulations cross-linguistically.

examples.note: Proto-Slavic consonants before front vowels became palatalized in East Slavic; the palatalized series is now phonemic in Russian.
'milk'; palatalized before the front diphthong ie
The plural ending /i/ palatalizes the final consonant and is deleted.
The second-person singular ending /i/ behaves the same way.
